label: the forms haa/hii/he and to/tii/te, in all three genders
note: Chapter 69. Two fronts and three endings make six words: ha- for near, ta- for far, with -aa / -ii / -e chosen by the noun's gender rather than by the speaker. Taught on mitra, kholi and ghar, whose genders are STATED in the corpus (MR-C41-kholi says ghar is neuter and kholi feminine; maajhaa mitra gives the masculine) rather than assumed -- chahaa was dropped from a draft because its gender is nowhere stated.
